items.title: Chevron Cut Its Debt by $8.4 Billion. These 4 Dividend Stocks Have Fortress Balance Sheets
items.summary: When the next recession hits, only some dividends survive the squeeze. Four companies from four different sectors passed a strict balance sheet test, but one of them carries a red flag that makes retirees look twice.

items.title: Energy Stocks Benefit From Supply Disruptions: Can Momentum Last?
items.summary: Rising crude prices and diesel shortages drive gains for Valero, Cheniere, Chevron and ExxonMobil, but recovering oil supplies could test their momentum.

items.title: Bad News for Exxon and Chevron: Goldman Sees Brent Falling “Roughly $10” Next Year on a Supply Glut
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGoldman Sachs expects Brent and WTI crude to fall about $10 over the next year on an oil surplus of about 2 million barrels a day. Consensus estimates for ExxonMobil, Chevron and ConocoPhillips still reflect this year’s wartime oil prices.

items.title: Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Collect Billions From These Untouchable Berkshire Hathaway Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Five Berkshire holdings never budged in the latest 13F, yet their yields range from a sliver to a hefty payout. Which ones actually deliver income for retirees, and which carry risks that could trim the checks?

items.title: Can Chevron Build a Lithium Business in the Smackover Formation?
items.summary: CVX is putting its oil and gas expertise to work in lithium, targeting opportunities in energy storage, from electric vehicle batteries to power grids.

items.title: Chevron Pays a Bigger Dividend, but Exxon May Be the Better Retirement Stock
items.summary: One oil giant hands retirees a bigger check today, while the other has kept raising its payout through every crash. When crude collapses again, which dividend will you wish you owned?

items.title: Why Chevron Investors Could Make Sense Of ETFs Now
items.summary: You might like Chevron for its global energy reach, but owning the stock directly means carrying its specific risks by yourself. Simply Wall St highlights one of those: that earnings are forecast to decline an average of 5.2% per year over the next 3 years. Holding Chevron through a fund that also owns other businesses spreads how much those company specific issues can swing your portfolio, and also spreads out how much its success can help you.
